questions.q: Course 6 already covered the classic business rule infinite-loop mistake. What is it, in one sentence?
options: A business rule that updates the same table it's triggered on, without excluding the change it itself just made, so the update re-triggers the rule
A business rule that is scheduled to run at midnight every day
A business rule that has no condition script at all
A business rule that only runs for the admin role
questions.explain: This is the recap: a business rule re-saving the record it's triggered on, without a guard, can re-trigger itself through that same save.

questions.q:
A debug panel shows:
*** Script: Business Rule "Calculate Priority Score" (incident) - 14 ms
*** Script: Business Rule "Calculate Priority Score" (incident) - 14 ms
*** Script: Business Rule "Calculate Priority Score" (incident) - 11 ms
*** Script: Business Rule "Calculate Priority Score" (incident) - 9 ms
*** Script: Business Rule "Calculate Priority Score" (incident) - 0 ms
for one form save. What is the real detection signature here?
options: One of the five lines is unusually slow
The business rule's name is misspelled
The same business rule name appears repeatedly for a single user action, with durations shrinking toward zero
The five lines represent five different business rules
questions.explain: Recursive triggers often aren't individually slow — the tell is the repeated count for one action, converging toward zero as the recalculated value stabilizes.

options: calculateScore() is undefined
current.update() performs a brand-new save on the same table, which other update business rules — including this one — are eligible to run on again
The function is missing a return statement
previous is never used in the script
questions.explain: current.update() is a real save on the incident table; ServiceNow treats it like any other update, so update business rules can fire on it again.

options: The idempotent guard skips the save entirely when nothing changed; setWorkflow(false) stops the remaining save from re-triggering business rules on the table
Both lines do the same thing and one is redundant
setWorkflow(false) deletes the record instead of updating it
The guard check has no effect on business rule execution count
questions.explain: The guard prevents unnecessary saves outright; setWorkflow(false) prevents the save that does happen from re-firing business rules, workflows, or flows.

questions.q: After deploying the fix, how do you confirm it actually worked?
options: Assume it worked because the code change matches the documented pattern
Delete the business rule and see if anything breaks
Turn on Debug Business Rule again, repeat the same save, and confirm the rule now fires exactly once
Raise the Slow Request Log's response-time threshold so it stops logging the transaction
questions.explain: Confirming a fix means re-measuring the same transaction with the same profiler that found the problem, not just trusting the code change.
